dedupe_keys.name: replication package for multi objective healthcare facility resilience planning texas 3 752 hospitals and nursing homes tropical cyclone flood scenarios hardening restoration and evacuation costs and social vulnerability weights

description: This replication package holds the inputs and results of a study that plans flood protection and patient evacuation for every hospital and nursing home in Texas together. It was deposited on Zenodo by Toplu-Tutay, Kammer-Kerwick, Hasenbein and Kutanoglu of The University of Texas at Austin, with the model code in a linked GitHub repository. The inputs cover 3,752 facilities with locations, bed capacities and occupancy; flood scenarios derived from 27 tropical cyclones that struck Texas between 1993 and 2018, in a main set and a percentile-based set; costs of hardening each facility, of restoring it after flooding and of moving patients between facilities; and census-tract social vulnerability used to weight service disruption. The outputs include run records, trade-off frontiers and decision variables from a two-stage stochastic model solved by Benders decomposition and a Lagrangian-dual method, with value-of-information analyses. The package is free and available to download under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the code repository could not be read from this environment, the cost and scenario inputs are modelling assumptions, not observed values, and coverage is limited to Texas. Simulation uses: testing hospital hardening and evacuation strategies against hurricane flooding, benchmarking optimisation methods, and reusing the facility, cost and scenario tables in other exposure studies. Related records: the CMS provider data on hospitals (data-cms-provider-data-hospitals) gives the national facility register such studies start from.
